chapterTitle: FBISE Full-Book Annual Exam Simulator III (Comprehensive All Units 10–18)
subject: biology-10

questions.question: Which cartilaginous structure houses the vocal cords and produces the human voice? (FBISE Annual 2024)
questions.explanation: The larynx contains vibrating vocal cords that produce sound modulated into speech by tongue, lips, and pharynx.

questions.question: What is the primary chemical composition of approximately 70% of human kidney stones (renal calculi)? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: The majority of renal calculi are composed of insoluble calcium oxalate precipitates formed in supersaturated urine.

questions.question: The primary auditory sensory organ containing hair cells that transduce sound vibrations into nerve impulses in the inner ear is the:

options.B: Organ of Corti in the cochlea

questions.explanation: The organ of Corti resting on the cochlear basilar membrane contains mechanoreceptive hair cells that generate acoustic nerve impulses.

questions.question: The small triangular sesamoid bone that forms the kneecap protecting the anterior knee joint is the: (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: The patella (kneecap) is embedded within the quadriceps tendon to shield the knee and optimize extensor leverage.

questions.question: In flowering plants, successful fertilization results in the transformation of the ovule into a seed and the ovary into a: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Following fertilization, the ovary wall ripens into the pericarp of the fruit, enclosing the mature seeds.

questions.question: If a red-flowered plant is crossed with a white-flowered plant of Mirabilis jalapa, all F1 offspring have pink flowers due to: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance produces an intermediate blended phenotype (pink flowers, Rr) in heterozygous offspring.

questions.question: The conversion of atmospheric nitrogen gas (N2) into biologically usable ammonia by soil microbes is termed: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Biological nitrogen fixation (by Rhizobium, Azotobacter, cyanobacteria) breaks the triple bond of N2 to form ammonia.

questions.question: The progressive accumulation of persistent non-biodegradable synthetic chemical toxins (e.g., DDT) at higher trophic levels is:
questions.explanation: Biomagnification concentrates lipophilic persistent contaminants progressively up each step of a food chain.

questions.question: Bt cotton crops carry a crystalline endotoxin gene isolated from which soil bacterium to resist insect pests? (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis produces Cry endotoxins that disrupt insect larval gut membranes, providing biological pest resistance.

questions.question: Which category of addictive drugs includes morphine, codeine, and heroin, which relieve severe pain but cause high physical dependence?
questions.explanation: Narcotics (opioids) bind central opioid receptors to dull severe pain, carrying high risks of tolerance and physical dependence.

questions.question: Why are antibiotics completely ineffective in treating viral illnesses such as influenza and the common cold? (FBISE 2022)

options.A: Viruses lack cell walls, ribosomes, and metabolic machinery targeted by antibiotics
options.B: Viruses destroy antibiotics in the blood
options.C: Viruses are too small to touch antibiotics

questions.explanation: Antibiotics selectively target bacterial cell walls, prokaryotic ribosomes, or bacterial enzymes absent in acellular viruses.

questions.question: The clinical technique that introduces a functional gene to replace or supplement a mutated disease-causing gene in a patient is: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Gene therapy delivers healthy, therapeutic genetic alleles directly into target patient cells to correct underlying genetic disorders.
